the polymerase chain (PCR) was useful in the detection of eae gene of SLT- E. coli.
a PCR assay was developed for the detection of the eae genes of Shiga-like-toxin-producing Escherichiacoli (SLT- EC).

a PCR method for detection of the eae (EAF) gene of SLT- E. coli was developed, and that the PCR products generated by this method were used to characterize the EAF gene in a large number of human, porcine, and bovine SLT-EC.

the development of a PCR-based assay for the detection of the eae genes of human and bovine SLT-EC.
the use of the PCR for the detection of the eae genes in SLT-EC and for the characterization of the eaa genes from these organisms.
the detection and characterization of the 5' and 3' ends of the eae genes of SLT-ec using PCR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the eae gene was detected in most SLT-EC from human and bovine sources, but the gene was not present in the majority of porcine strains examined.
the PCR method used is a useful technique for the rapid detection of the eae genes from a wide variety of SLT-ec strains and is a potentially useful epidemiological tool.

the PCR assay for eae described in this study is useful for the detection of SLT- EC strains from humans and cattle and is a rapid and reliable method for the characterization of SLT- E. coli strains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the eae gene appears to be a relatively specific marker for human and bovine SLT-EC, and the 3' portion of eae is more useful for the detection of SLT- EC O serogroups than the 5' region of the eae sequence.
PCR using the eae prim ers described herein appears to be a rapid and sensitive method for the detection and characterization of SLT- EC strains from humans and cattle.
the eae gene was found in the majority of the SLT-producing E. coli strains of the O serogroups tested, but the gene was not found in non-SLT- EC strains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to develop a PCR-based assay that could distinguish SLT-EC from other enteric bacterial pathogens.
we have shown that the E. coli eae gene is a good candidate for use as a PCR target in a DNA probe to detect SLT-EC in clinical samples.
we were able to use PCR to detect the eae gene from a large proportion of SLT- EC strains, and we were also able to distinguish among SLT-EC isolates from different O serogroups.
